claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa material has a single-phase BCC dendritic structure.
Adding a controlled amount of Zr to TiVNbTa can improve its high-temperature mechanical stability.
Adding Zr to TiVNbTa can improve heat-transfer efficiency.
Zr additions will provide solid-solution strengthening in TiVNbTa.
Zr addition will produce precipitates or secondary phases.
The precipitates or secondary phases will impede dislocation motion.
The proposed improvement operates through solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed improvement also operates through grain-boundary strengthening.
Zr-modified TiVNbTa will have improved high-temperature yield strength.
Zr-modified TiVNbTa will have improved high-temperature compressive strength.
The strength of Zr-modified TiVNbTa may exceed 500 MPa at 1273 K.
The predicted strength improvement will involve minimal loss of ductility.
The reported TiVNbTa baseline at 1273 K is 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain.
The proposed operating-temperature boundary is 873–1373 K.
The proposed loading boundary extends to 50% strain.

contradictions.description: The intervention is framed as solid-solution strengthening, whereas the structural mediator is precipitation or formation of secondary phases. These are distinct strengthening states, and the hypothesis does not specify which state is intended or how both coexist.

The stated mediator can explain precipitation-based obstruction of dislocations, but it does not establish the claimed grain-boundary strengthening because no grain-size or grain-boundary modification is specified.
